prompts.01-Foot:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one 16 by 16 pixel tile for a top-down 2D RPG mountain tileset, shown as a square nearest-neighbor enlarged image.
Reference image 1: user's visual reference ONLY for the upright, nearly 90-degree brown cliff, angular rock planes and chunky pixel-art style. Do not reproduce its tree, green scenery, cursor or screenshot framing.
Reference image 2: existing project grass color swatch, exact #89A043.
The tile fills the ENTIRE square with NO margin, frame, grid lines, tile divisions, writing, checkerboard or transparency. Exactly 16 logical pixels across and 16 down. Every logical pixel is a perfectly uniform square, all same size. No subpixel detail, antialiasing, gradients, blur, brush texture or lighting effects.
Use ONLY this subdued flat palette: rock base #A08043, lighter rock plane and summit #B3995C, rock shadow #805B32, occasional deep vertical crevice #514332, ground grass #89A043, grass contact shadow #647B36.
Mountain rock must read as a tall continuous cliff face with 2 or 3 large elongated angular planes and sparse narrow vertical cracks, like reference. NOT a pile of stones, boulders, bricks, cobblestones, a wooden fence, stepped terraces or rounded rocks. Keep large quiet color clusters, no dithering or decorative scattered pixels. No bright/specular highlights.
This single tile will be stacked into a vertical mountain cross-section in this top-to-bottom order: far summit edge / solid summit / front summit-to-wall fold / wall / foot / grass. Generate ONLY the specific tile described next.
Requested tile: FRONT MOUNTAIN FOOT. Rock wall fills upper 12 logical pixel rows (75% height); existing grass fills bottom 4 logical rows (25%). The upright wall meets horizontal grass at an almost 90-degree bend, along a mostly horizontal subtly jagged contact edge. No mountain-top surface is visible. Uppermost row is entirely #A08043 to connect to the wall tile above. Rock face has sparse long vertical angular fissures, not separate outlined stones. End the rock around logical row 11; row 12 is a thin broken #647B36 contact shadow, bottom rows 13-15 are uninterrupted EXACT #89A043 so they seamlessly meet the existing grass tile. Texture does not reach the left/right crop edges as a border; the cliff continues sideways.
Reference image 3: generated wall texture from this same set, used ONLY as matching style and brown palette reference. Simplify it to a TRUE 16x16 logical pixel design (not 32x32), no small steps. Keep the specific requested tile composition; do not output the whole wall for every tile. Flat fill colors, no mottling or gradient. Seam interface rows must be uniform as specified.
